zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left (or right) of Y, enforce that X's house index is less than (or greater than) Y's index.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains the phrase 'to the left of' or 'to the right of' without the word 'directly'.
zebralogic.example: Placing X to the right of Y despite a clue stating X is somewhere to the left of Y.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., 'Arnold is the person whose birthday is in January'), treat them as the same entity across categories.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses linking verbs such as 'is', 'are', or 'equals' to connect two values.
zebralogic.example: Assigning Arnold a birthday other than January despite the clue linking them.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, enforce that exact placement and treat it as a hard constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house number (e.g., 'in the fifth house', 'house 2').
zebralogic.example: Ignoring 'Eric is in the fifth house' and placing Eric in another house.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: The solution JSON must be the very last part of the response with no extra characters after it; otherwise the verifier may not capture the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After all reasoning is complete, output only the JSON and stop.
zebralogic.example: Adding a concluding sentence after the JSON, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house, enforce that the attribute cannot occupy that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains 'not in house X' or similar negation.
zebralogic.example: Placing Alice in house 2 despite the clue 'Alice is not in house 2'.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B and B = C), propagate the equivalence to link all related values directly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After processing all equivalence clues, compute the transitive closure of linked values.
zebralogic.example: Knowing Arnold = Jan and Jan = knitting but failing to also assign Arnold = master education.

zebralogic.title: ExactAttributeValueMatching
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling, case, and formatting.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final JSON or any intermediate assignment.
zebralogic.example: Writing 'apr' instead of the required 'april' for a birthday month.

zebralogic.title: LimitReasoningLength
zebralogic.principle: Keep reasoning concise enough to stay within the model's token budget; avoid overly verbose explanations that may be truncated.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the solution process, especially before the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Providing a long, detailed narrative that exceeds the token limit, causing the verifier to miss the JSON.

zebralogic.title: HouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue specifies a concrete number of houses between X and Y, enforce that there are exactly that many houses separating them (|pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains phrases like 'N houses between' or 'N houses apart'.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'two houses between X and Y' as X being two houses away from Y, resulting in only one house separating them.

zebralogic.title: OverlappingAttributeDisambiguation
zebralogic.principle: When a term appears in multiple attribute categories, use contextual cues (verbs, surrounding words) to determine the correct category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During clue parsing whenever a word could belong to more than one attribute set.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'high school' as a hobby instead of an education level.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart'
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The phrasing is ambiguous; the model often treats the number as a simple distance rather than counting the houses that lie strictly between the two.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Translate the clue into a constraint that there must be exactly N distinct houses separating X and Y, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing the verifier to miss the answer
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate explanatory text after outputting the JSON, not realizing the verifier stops parsing at the first JSON block.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output the JSON as the final token sequence and terminate the response immediately.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the verifier to truncate
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Generating overly long reasoning exceeds the model's token budget, leading to truncation before the JSON.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise and stop before reaching the token limit; prioritize the final answer.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Negative clues are sometimes treated as optional or overlooked during deduction.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat any 'not in house X' statement as a hard exclusion constraint.

zebralogic.description: Confusing overlapping attribute values across categories
zebralogic.why_it_happens: When a term can belong to multiple attribute sets, the model may assign it to the wrong category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Use contextual verbs and clue structure to disambiguate which attribute category a term belongs to.
